analyzed_vuln.description: The UAF is caused by an invalid generational-to-full-GC transition. `mrb_full_gc()` enters `clear_all_old()`, whose `gc->full == FALSE` path switches off generational mode and starts sweeping directly with `prepare_incremental_sweep()`, rather than first completing/restarting a full root-and-child mark. Under the PoV's allocation pressure, this allows a heap page containing an object still referenced by an instance-variable table (the generated `@scope` chain) to be classified as wholly dead and released in `incremental_sweep_phase()`. The IV entry remains dangling. A later forced full GC traverses that IV table and `mrb_gc_mark()` reads the freed RVALUE at gc.c:743. The page-free operation is only where the bad GC state manifests; the vulnerable state transition is in `clear_all_old()`.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: The protobuf converter emits a very large allocation-heavy Ruby program with nested `@scope ||= begin ... end` expressions and many Array combination/permutation operations, creating enough objects to exercise generational/incremental GC. It then emits many `ObjectSpace.count_objects` calls. Each call reaches `os_count_objects()` -> `mrb_objspace_each_objects()` -> `mrb_full_gc()`. When a forced full collection occurs after a minor-generational cycle (`gc->full == FALSE`), `clear_all_old()` takes its direct-sweep branch; a reachable object referenced from an IV table can then have its entire heap page freed. A subsequent `ObjectSpace.count_objects` forces another mark, follows the stale IV value, and triggers the heap-use-after-free in `mrb_gc_mark()`.
